newsitem.title: USA: Huntco sees higher sales, lower margins.
newsitem.headline: Huntco sees higher sales, lower margins.

text.p: Huntco Inc said Monday it expects net sales for its fiscal 1998 year to increase by about 20 percent over fiscal 1997 net sales of $326.6 million.

The company, an intermediate steel processor specializing in the processing of flat rolled carbon steel, also said it expects fiscal 1998 second quarter net sales to show an increase near the 20 percent increase expected for the year. Last year, Huntco reported second quarter sales of $84 million.

Huntco said it expects its gross profit margins in the second quarter of fiscal 1998 could decline somewhat due to cold rolled steel price competition, likely ranging from 9.0 percent to 10.0 percent of net sales.

Earlier today, the company reported earnings for its fiscal 1998 first quarter ended July 31, 1997 fell to $1.8 million or $0.20 a share from $2.6 million or $0.29 in the same period last year. Net sales for the quarter were $90.5 million, up 15.4 percent from the $78.4 million in the prior year's first quarter.

Gross profit shown as percent of net sales was 10.0 percent for the quarter ended July 31, 1997, which compares to 11.5 percent for the quarter ended July 31, 1996 and 9.0 percent for the quarter ended April 30, 1997.

Higher net sales reflected increased levels of tons processed, primarily at new facilities in Kentucky, which opened in July, 1996, and South Carolina, which opened in January, 1997, and at its cold rolling operation at its Blytheville facility.
Huntco said it processed and shipped a record 266,595 tons of steel in the first quarter ended July 31, 1997, up 15.3 percent from the first quarter ended July 31, 1996.
